sections.html:
Bossier Parish sits in northwest Louisiana on the east side of the Red River, directly across from Shreveport. Its 2020 population was 128,746, and the 2025 estimate is 131,867. Bossier City is the largest municipality, and Benton is the parish seat, where the courthouse and the assessor's office are found. Haughton and Plain Dealing are the other towns.

Barksdale Air Force Base, about four miles east of Bossier City, anchors the local housing market, and the parish is part of the Shreveport-Bossier City metro area. Age and condition still decide how a buyer prices an older house.

sections.h2: Who assesses and who collects property tax
sections.html:
The Bossier Parish Assessor appraises every parcel, and the Bossier Parish Sheriff collects the tax. The assessor's office is at 204 Burt Boulevard, 2nd Floor, in Benton, open Monday to Friday from 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM, closed on state holidays. The phone is (318) 965-2213.

The assessor posts a SmartCAMA property search and a GIS aerial map, which let an owner look up a parcel's assessment and ownership before calling. The assessor does not take payment. Pay the Sheriff.

  • Online: the "Pay Taxes" tab at bossiersheriff.com, using the tax assessment number and the owner's last name as printed on the notice. A mobile app offers the same service.
  • By mail: Sheriff's Office, P.O. Box 850, Benton, LA 71006.
  • In person: the Bossier Parish Courthouse at 204 Burt Boulevard, the Viking Drive Substation at 2510 Viking Drive in Bossier City, or the Arthur Ray Teague Substation at 3135 Arthur Ray Teague Parkway in Bossier City, all open 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM on business days.

The tax year runs from a January 1 lien date to a December 31 payment deadline. The open book period and the appeal dates move with the calendar, so ask the assessor for the current year's days.

Yearly property tax calendar in Bossier Parish
WhenWhat happens
January 1Lien date
April 1Business personal property self-reporting deadline
Late AugustOpen book period, about two weeks
Early SeptemberDeadline to appeal an assessment to the Board of Review (Bossier Parish Police Jury)
The following weekBoard of Review hearing

sections.h2: Home value and the homestead exemption
sections.html:
Louisiana assesses land and residential improvements at 10% of market value, and the parish tax is then the assessed value times your millage. Commercial improvements are assessed at 15%.

The homestead exemption exempts the first $75,000 of parish value. Call the assessor at 318-965-2213 to file. The assessor's exemptions page also lists relief for disabled veteran owners and other programs, and the SmartCAMA system shows codes for a senior citizen freeze for those over 65 and for a delayed homestead application.

Before a sale, ask the assessor what exemptions are attached to the file, since an exemption tied to the seller as the occupant will not carry over to a buyer.

sections.h2: How to appeal a Bossier Parish assessment
sections.html:
Review the value during the open book period in late August, then file an appeal with the Board of Review by the early September deadline. The board is the Bossier Parish Police Jury, and it hears cases about a week later.

Come with comparable sales, photos of any damage and any repair estimate. The assessor's office can walk you through its records first. If either side disagrees with the board, the case can continue to the Louisiana Tax Commission, and the Bossier office can explain how that step works.

sections.h2: How does the new Louisiana tax lien process affect an owner?
sections.html:
Since January 1, 2026, Bossier's tax collector no longer sells the property itself for unpaid ad valorem tax. The auction now offers a tax lien certificate that represents the delinquent taxes, interest, penalties and costs. The unpaid tax liability is sold and a lien goes to the buyer, but the property is not sold.

  • Interest can run up to 1% per month without compounding, plus a penalty of up to 5%.
  • The certificate is recorded after the auction, and the owner can still pay until 30 days after service of a petition to enforce the lien.
  • The holder may file suit only after the later of three years from recording or 180 days after the required notices under R.S. 47:2156.

Louisiana Revised Statutes sections 47:2153 and 47:2155 set the notice and certificate rules. Contact the tax collector or an attorney about redemption and enforcement. The certificate is recorded, so it has to be cleared at any sale.

The tax for the year stays with the property until someone pays it, so check it before you sign anything. Ask the Sheriff's tax office for the account balance, look for any recorded tax lien certificate, and ask the assessor whether a homestead exemption is attached to the file.

Foreclosure is a separate matter. The Sheriff also runs real estate foreclosure sales, which are listed on its own page, with online bidding handled through Bid4Assets. A homeowner who is behind on a mortgage as well as on tax should read the notices on both lists, because the two processes run on different timelines.

A seller with several problems at once, such as an unfinished repair, a tenant in place and a tax balance, can still sell to a cash buyer who takes the house as-is. The title company pays off the tax from the proceeds at the table, so the sale price must be enough to cover the balance, the mortgage and any lien.

sections.h2: Steps before you list a Bossier Parish house
sections.html:
Work through a short checklist before you accept an offer. First, look up the parcel on the assessor's SmartCAMA search to confirm the owner name, the assessment and any exemption codes. Second, call the Sheriff's tax office for the balance on this year's account and ask whether a tax lien certificate has been recorded against it. Third, if you carry a mortgage, check whether escrow paid the tax and get proof.

Put those answers in front of your closing agent early. The payoff comes out of the proceeds at the table, and a recorded certificate has to be cleared before the buyer gets clean title. If you plan to dispute the value, remember that the open book period is short and the appeal deadline follows within days, so the time to call the assessor is before the books open.

After the sale, the buyer should ask the assessor to update the ownership record and apply for a homestead exemption in their own name. Your exemption does not move with the house.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property tax to in Bossier Parish?
faqs.a: You pay the Bossier Parish Sheriff, who acts as tax collector. Payment can be made online at bossiersheriff.com, by mail to P.O. Box 850, Benton, LA 71006, or in person at the courthouse in Benton or at the two Bossier City substations.

faqs.q: When is the Bossier Parish appeal deadline?
faqs.a: The open book period runs in late August, and the appeal to the Board of Review is due in early September, with the hearing about a week later. Call the assessor at (318) 965-2213 for the exact days.

faqs.q: When are Bossier Parish property taxes due?
faqs.a: Property taxes are due on December 31 each year.

faqs.q: How much does the Bossier homestead exemption cover?
faqs.a: It exempts the first $75,000 of parish value. Call the assessor at 318-965-2213 to file.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Bossier Parish house with a tax balance?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company can pay the delinquent tax from the proceeds at closing. Get the payoff from the Sheriff and ask whether a lien certificate has been recorded.
